content: It is not suffering itself that destroys human beings, but suffering without purpose.
author: Viktor Frankl
sourceWork: Yes to Life: In Spite of Everything (1946)
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Hardship is not an unfair interruption to your real life—it is the very forge in which character is tempered. No one develops deep wisdom, empathy, or stamina by cruising down an easy path without resistance.

Across his life and work, Viktor Frankl saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Like a tree that develops deeper roots when buffeted by winter gales, your past trials gave you a reservoir of strength you didn't know you possessed. You are more durable than your anxious thoughts give you credit for.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
